guide-section: "Package Comparisons"
---

This page runs the same competing-risks example at the same five horizons in
three implementations. The estimates agree after rounding; what differs is the
API and the shape of the returned result.

## Shared example

Each row is one observation. Code `0` means right-censored, `1` is the event of
interest, and `2` is the competing event.

| `times` | 24.1 | 9.7 | 49.9 | 18.6 | 34.8 | 14.2 | 39.2 | 46.0 | 31.5 | 4.3 |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `reals` | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 0 | 2 | 1 | 2 | 0 | 1 |

::: {.panel-tabset}

## polarstate (Python)

`polarstate` prepares one inspectable event table, then returns all state
probabilities together.

```python
import polars as pl
from polarstate import prepare_event_table, predict_aj_estimates

data = pl.DataFrame({
    "times": [24.1, 9.7, 49.9, 18.6, 34.8, 14.2, 39.2, 46.0, 31.5, 4.3],
    "reals": [1, 1, 1, 1, 0, 2, 1, 2, 0, 1],
})

event_table = prepare_event_table(data)

predict_aj_estimates(
    event_table,
    pl.Series([10.0, 20.0, 30.0, 40.0, 50.0]),
).select(
    pl.col("times"),
    pl.col("state_occupancy_probability_0").alias("event_free"),
    pl.col("state_occupancy_probability_1").alias("primary_event"),
    pl.col("state_occupancy_probability_2").alias("competing_event"),
)
```

Rounded output:

| time | event-free | primary event | competing event |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 10 | 0.800000 | 0.200000 | 0.000000 |
| 20 | 0.600000 | 0.300000 | 0.100000 |
| 30 | 0.500000 | 0.400000 | 0.100000 |
| 40 | 0.333333 | 0.566667 | 0.100000 |
| 50 | 0.000000 | 0.733333 | 0.266667 |

## lifelines (Python)

`lifelines` fits one
[AalenJohansenFitter](https://lifelines.readthedocs.io/en/latest/fitters/univariate/AalenJohansenFitter.html)
per event type. Combining the two predictions makes the comparison explicit.

```python
import pandas as pd
from lifelines import AalenJohansenFitter

data = pd.DataFrame({
    "times": [24.1, 9.7, 49.9, 18.6, 34.8, 14.2, 39.2, 46.0, 31.5, 4.3],
    "reals": [1, 1, 1, 1, 0, 2, 1, 2, 0, 1],
})
horizons = [10.0, 20.0, 30.0, 40.0, 50.0]

primary = AalenJohansenFitter(calculate_variance=False)
primary.fit(data["times"], data["reals"], event_of_interest=1)

competing = AalenJohansenFitter(calculate_variance=False)
competing.fit(data["times"], data["reals"], event_of_interest=2)

comparison = pd.DataFrame({
    "time": horizons,
    "primary_event": primary.predict(horizons).to_numpy(),
    "competing_event": competing.predict(horizons).to_numpy(),
})
comparison
```

Rounded output:

| time | primary event | competing event |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 10 | 0.200000 | 0.000000 |
| 20 | 0.300000 | 0.100000 |
| 30 | 0.400000 | 0.100000 |
| 40 | 0.566667 | 0.100000 |
| 50 | 0.733333 | 0.266667 |

## tidycmprsk (R)

`tidycmprsk` returns outcome-specific estimates in a tidy table. The final
pivot only places the two outcomes side by side.

```r
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(tidycmprsk)

data <- tibble(
  times = c(24.1, 9.7, 49.9, 18.6, 34.8, 14.2, 39.2, 46.0, 31.5, 4.3),
  reals = factor(
    c(1, 1, 1, 1, 0, 2, 1, 2, 0, 1),
    levels = c(0, 1, 2),
    labels = c("censored", "primary_event", "competing_event")
  )
)
horizons <- c(10, 20, 30, 40, 50)

fit <- cuminc(Surv(times, reals) ~ 1, data)

tidy(fit, time = horizons) |>
  select(outcome, time, estimate) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = outcome, values_from = estimate)
```

Rounded output:

| time | primary event | competing event |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 10 | 0.200000 | 0.000000 |
| 20 | 0.300000 | 0.100000 |
| 30 | 0.400000 | 0.100000 |
| 40 | 0.566667 | 0.100000 |
| 50 | 0.733333 | 0.266667 |

See the official
[`cuminc()` documentation](https://mskcc-epi-bio.github.io/tidycmprsk/reference/cuminc.html)
and
[tidying methods](https://mskcc-epi-bio.github.io/tidycmprsk/reference/broom_methods_cuminc.html)
for the complete R API.

:::

## What differs?

| Package | Typical result | Practical distinction |
|---|---|---|
| `polarstate` | One Polars table with all three state probabilities | Separates event-table preparation from horizon lookup |
| `lifelines` | One pandas result per event of interest | Fits an Aalen-Johansen object separately for each event type |
| `tidycmprsk` | Outcome-specific rows in a tidy R table | Uses an R formula interface and factor-coded outcomes |

For data with no competing event, use only codes `0` and `1` in `polarstate`;
the competing-event probability remains zero. See [Recipes](05-recipes.qmd)
for that shorter pattern.
